detail: button[disabled]{opacity:.45} composited answered quiz option text to 3.36:1 against the white card, below the WCAG 2.2 AA 4.5:1 body-text minimum. Answered options are primary reading content after submission, so the disabled-control exception does not apply. The generated a11y report had claimed this check passed.
evidence: composite contrast calculation: 45% ink over white = #8C8C8C = 3.36:1
action: removed blanket opacity; answered options keep ink on white at 21:1, disabled controls use --muted on --oatmeal at 10.26:1
prevention: never express a disabled state with opacity on text that remains readable content; lint checks token pairs and cannot see composited alpha, so verify disabled states in a real browser

detail: The standalone localStorage fallback wrote unscoped cmi.* keys. Because every module in a package set is served from one origin, opening a second module inherited the first module's saved position, status, and score. BLD-102 opened at 80 percent on a first visit after FND-104 had been completed.
evidence: manual browser verification: BLD-102 resumed at 80% on first open at http://127.0.0.1:8000/BLD-102/index.html
regression test reproduces it: cross-module isolation check in tools/agents/runtime_qa.js
decided_by: runtime and regression qa (manual browser pass)
action: namespaced fallback keys as scorm:<module_id>:<key>; real LMS key names are unchanged
prevention: when a runtime persists state outside an LMS, scope the keys per module and test two modules against one shared store - a per-module harness cannot see cross-module leakage

detail: Every correct answer was option 1 in all quiz items and checkpoints. The shared paged runtime renders options in authored order and never shuffles, so a learner could pass by always choosing the first option. Same pattern found in FND-104 specs.
evidence: headless browser pass: OPS-107 SCR-09 correct option rendered first
action: place_correct() in specs_support.py rotates correct positions deterministically; option ids unchanged so key.json still resolves
prevention: audit correct-answer position distribution before packaging any paged module; the shared runtime does not shuffle

detail: runtime_qa.js selects quiz options by the first 25 characters of text; identical or prefix-sharing options across items (for example 'The Feedback and Ideas board.' and 'Urgent.') made the harness click the wrong item, so all-correct scored 60.
evidence: runtime_qa.js: OPS-108 SCR-10 all-correct score was 60; OPS-107 submit disabled with all answered
action: rewrote colliding options to be distinct and self-describing
prevention: keep every option's first 25 characters unique across a quiz; short one-word options also read poorly out of context
